evidence.claim: Niagara Falls began at the escarpment between Lewiston and Queenston, downstream of the present falls.
evidence.quote: The Niagara River intersects the Niagara Escarpment between Lewiston and Queenston, Ontario, identifying the escarpment's Lewiston-Queenston section as the geologic origin of Niagara Falls.

evidence.claim: Over roughly 12,500 years, erosion moved the falls nearly seven miles south, leaving the Niagara Gorge.
evidence.quote: Over a roughly 12,500 year span, the falls have eroded nearly seven miles south from Lewiston to their present location in Niagara Falls, creating the seven-mile long Niagara Gorge.

evidence.claim: The escarpment also shaped transport: in 1764, British military engineer John Montresor built an inclined wooden tramway here.
evidence.quote: an inclined wooden tramway built here in 1764 by John Montresor (1736–1799), a British military engineer.

evidence.claim: Loaded carts climbed wooden rails, pulled by rope, to move goods over the escarpment.
evidence.quote: it featured loaded carts pulled up wooden rails by rope. It promoted the movement of goods over the Niagara Escarpment in present-day Lewiston.

evidence.claim: The village lies on the Niagara River across from Canada, between Niagara Falls and Fort Niagara.
evidence.quote: Lewiston lies halfway between the world-famous Niagara Falls and historic Fort Niagara in Youngstown.

evidence.claim: The village lies on the Niagara River across from Canada
evidence.quote: Lewiston is situated on the Niagara River, just across the river from Canada.

evidence.claim: Warship building transformed Sackets Harbor during the War of 1812.
evidence.quote: To support the War of 1812, the US Navy built a major shipyard and its headquarters for the Great Lakes at the village.

evidence.claim: The Navy established its Great Lakes headquarters and a major yard here, where more than 3,000 men worked.
evidence.quote: Within a short period, more than 3,000 men worked at the shipyard.

evidence.claim: Soldiers built defenses and camped in the village; by fall 1814, the combined population ranked behind only New York City and Albany in the state.
evidence.quote: By the fall of 1814, this was the third-largest population center in the entire state, after Albany and New York City.

evidence.claim: The war ended before the USS New Orleans was completed. Stored unfinished, it was finally scrapped in 1883.
evidence.quote: The end of the war came in 1815 before the Navy completed construction of the last warship, the USS New Orleans. She was put into storage and never completed. She was finally scrapped in 1883.

evidence.claim: Navy Point now serves private boats as a marina.
evidence.quote: Navy Point is a marina providing moorings and facilities for private boats.

evidence.claim: Soldiers built defenses and camped in the village
evidence.quote: The Army constructed earthworks, forts, barracks and supporting infrastructure to defend the village and navy shipyard, and its troops also camped in the village.

evidence.claim: The park’s first paved road arrived in 1924; Peninsula Drive now provides the main road approach, with 13 miles of roads within the park.
evidence.quote: The first paved road was built in the park in 1924, and today 13 miles (21 km) of roads run through the park. Pennsylvania Route 832 is the main road into the park, and is subsequently known as Peninsula Drive.

evidence.claim: The tramway was known as The Cradles and the Old Lewiston Incline, names for the rope-and-rail system that carried loads up the slope.
evidence.quote: Called "The Cradles" and "The Old Lewiston Incline," it featured loaded carts pulled up wooden rails by rope.

evidence.claim: The village’s Main Street and preserved 19th-century buildings form the Sackets Harbor Village Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.
evidence.quote: The heart of the village, with a Main Street and well-preserved 19th century buildings, has been recognized as the Sackets Harbor Village Historic District and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.

flags: Corrected current intro: the Ohio-border segment begins on US 20, not PA 5. PennDOT’s state-designated segment starts at the US 20/PA 5 junction; the interstate trail has a broader extent.
Wikipedia’s lead says first designation in 1978; its history says conceived in 1978, legislative designation in 1980 and first recognition in 1983. Retained conception date only.
The Wikipedia history describes the Pennsylvania extension as 50 miles, while its route section gives 64. Used FHWA’s 518-mile total and omitted extension mileage.
Lewiston page gives roughly 12,500 years in its opening and approximately 12,000 later. Retained the qualified opening figure; geology has no primary scientific source in this cache.
Dropped current undated Sackets Harbor population: 1,351 is a 2020 census figure, not a verified present count. Headquarters claim is supported but omitted for focus.
Detailed Niagara routing in Wikipedia uses older road names. Narrative uses geographic anchors rather than turn-by-turn directions.
